answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is adaptive per-identity proof-of-work calibrated to network gale. Each agent must solve a unique puzzle whose difficulty scales with recent gale (tx volume) and is keyed to a cedar root from the prior epoch beacon. Honest agents pay modest linear CPU cost. Attackers with many identities face superlinear cost because each puzzle is non-shareable and the delta in required sustained hash power grows with concurrent heads%2C forcing real dedicated hardware that cannot be amortized. Fake identities thus cost more than any expected reward.
